apparatus_basin_a00.claim_scope: Enrichment audit for a derived V2 apparatus basin using source-card/V2-row alignments. It tests whether the target basin is enriched for marker families; it does not prove physical equivalence or that all rows in the basin are Abelian mechanisms.

gamma_bridges.claim_scope: Gamma tokens are bridge-family codewords learned from V2 transfer-bridge candidate features. They are not proof of physical equivalence and do not by themselves solve a global GW transport plan.

recommendation.decision: Two primitive spaces with C/R/P as an attached completion fiber.

grammar_rules.claim_scope: Grammar-rule learner over deterministic V2 evidence matrices and typed edges. It selects a compact logical factorization for the language; it does not prove physical equivalence and does not replace source-card or decoder validation.

logical_compactness.interpretation: Compactness is hierarchical: Ω and Ξ are factor spaces; A, Π and table cells are derived indices. The language should not be collapsed to a single flat A vocabulary.

hierarchical_language.claim_scope: Hierarchical compilation of learned V2 symbolic artifacts. It defines how learned codebooks are composed into logical grammar layers; it does not prove physical equivalence or exact equation reconstruction.

grammar_rules.refined_apparatus_regime: A* := conditional_split(A_parent | Ω, Ξ, route, product_features)
grammar_rules.constructor_completion: DAG layer := monotone increase of constructor roles; transfer roads stay outside the DAG by default

claims_supported: The logical grammar is hierarchical, not a single overcompressed label set.
Ω and Ξ are the only primitive factor alphabets in the current V2 representation.
A is a derived apparatus regime over operator, substrate, route and edge-participation evidence.
Λ, T and Γ are distinct relation layers: typed roads, directed source-local transitions and bridge families.
Π is a repeated-transition motif layer; it should not be used as a replacement for T or Λ.
The full-assignment audit shows a broad A basin; use refined A as a derived sublayer rather than increasing primitive factor count.

readout_application_coverage.claim_scope: Coverage audit for V2 readout/protocol/application evidence. It tests extraction coverage and sparsity; it does not validate equation reconstruction or physical mechanisms.

source_card_alignment.claim_scope: Alignment between source equation cards and V2 feature rows by paper id plus equation overlap. It creates row ids needed to attach original equations to atlas/DAG/language objects.

source_constructor_graph.claim_scope: Source-grounded constructor graph over original equation cards. Edges are source-local construction order and role-completion changes. This is not the V2 constructor-completion DAG and not proof of physical causation.

source_language_examples.claim_scope: Examples attach original source equation cards to V2 symbolic-language assignments through conservative source-card/V2-row alignment. Equation-clean endpoint rates measure extraction sanitation; mechanism-role support rates test whether centroid-derived token names have matching source constructor evidence. Neither proves physical equivalence or exact mechanism reconstruction.

symbolic_full_assignment.claim_scope: Full assignment of learned V2 symbolic codebooks to retained rows and retained typed edges. This tests corpus-scale coverage and sample stability of the learned language; it is not a proof of physical equivalence or exact mechanism reconstruction.

symbolic_language.claim_scope: V2-native symbolic language learned from operator/substrate matrices, typed graph edges, directed sequence evidence and variational first-variation diagnostics. Tokens are machine language for mechanism construction, not human field names.

v2_dag.claim_scope: Graph-theoretic audit over V2 evidence features and typed graph edges. Directed edges are monotone constructor-completion candidates, not proof of physical causality.

To explore the potential effects of the existence of the Planck scale in quantum field theory, phenomenological approaches aimed at combining in the same framework the constancy of the speed of light and also an invariant maximum scale of energy, $E_P=\ c/l_P$, have been considered in recent years under the name of deformed or doubly special relativity (DSR) \ . A DSR theory can be constructed assuming that the Lorentz group acts non-linearly on the components of the 4-momentum of a particle in such a way that the energy and/or momentum of the particle never become larger than a given scale (of order $\ E_P$). However, despite extensive theoretical and experimental research on distributed quantum sensing for photonic quantum sensors (see, e.g.,~\ for reviews), the asymptotic performance limits for function estimation are not yet rigorously established. Here, we close this gap, proving an ultimate bound on asymptotic performance, as measured by the mean square error of the estimator, for measuring a linear function of unknown parameters each coupled to a different photonic mode via either (1) the number operator $\ n$ or (2) a field-quadrature operator, chosen without loss of generality to be the momentum quadrature \\hat{p}:=i(\\hat{a}^\\dagger-\\hat{a})/2 . That is, we are interested in determining a function of either unknown local phase shifts or unknown quadrature displacements. For case (1), our primary focus, we derive this bound subject to a strict constraint on photon number, proving a long-standing conjecture appearing in Ref.~\ . In case (2), we derive our bound subject to a constraint on the average photon number, which is more natural in this setting as quadrature displacements are not photon-number conserving. Here, our results are consistent with existing bounds in the literature~\ , but, for completeness, we include derivations in this setting using an equivalent mathematical framework to the number operator case and the qubit sensor case~\ . source_examples.local_context: From Indefinite Causal Order to Quantum Skipping Skipping} Causal Order (ICO) is a counterintuitive phenomenon in quantum mechanics, arising when the order of operations on a system is placed into coherent superposition. In such scenarios, the sequence of events is no longer fixed. Quantum objects can undergo transformations where, in a well-defined sense, event A happens before B \ B happens before A.
